Hydra to provide 200 sample documents and two target pipelines (Priya) by 2026-01-17
Agree on success criteria and rollback thresholds in shared doc (both teams) by 2026-01-15
action_items: Priya Nair: upload 200 sample docs + 10 negative examples (due: 2026-01-17)

summary: POC kickoff to define quality evaluation plan: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, scoring approach, workload sizing and timeline. AE + SE from Redwood aligned on scoring buckets and benchmark cadence; Hydra to deliver sample data and acceptance criteria.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-10 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Attendees: Ariana Cho (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Hydra Head of ML), Samir Patel (Hydra Platform), Leah Morgan (Hydra Product)

[00:00] Ariana: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick agenda — align success criteria, map workload, and agree on a quality eval plan for the POC. Mateo will walk through the benchmark config.
[01:12] Priya: Thanks, yeah from our side we really want to validate hallucination rates and format adherence for two pipelines: clinical-summaries and regulatory Q&A. Primary metric is end-user correction rate — basically how often a human has to edit the model output.
[02:05] Mateo: Got it. For clarity, when you say correction rate, do you mean token-level edits or object-level (like whole-field fixes)?
[02:30] Priya: Mostly object-level — e.g., when a diagnosis field is wrong or a contraindication is hallucinated. But we'll capture token-level diffs as a secondary signal.
[03:10] Leah: Timeline check: we'd like results within 3 weeks if possible. Is that realistic?
[03:25] Ariana: Yes, 3 weeks is doable if we get sample data and golden prompts this week. We'll aim for initial benchmark run in week 2.
[04:05] Samir: Our infra: EKS cluster with A10G and some T4 for inference. We have a 95th percentile latency target of 300ms for single-turn queries in the consumer-facing pipeline. For the batch regulatory job latency is less strict.
[05:00] Mateo: Perfect — we'll size the workload accordingly. For the POC we suggest two load profiles: 1) interactive (p50/p95 latency targets, concurrency 40) 2) nightly batch (throughput 10k docs/hour). We'll include KV/prefix cache on the interactive profile.
[06:05] Priya: On scoring, we want a composite score: 50% correctness (object-level), 20% hallucination penalty, 20% format adherence, 10% latency/cost factor. Thoughts?
[06:30] Mateo: That weighting seems reasonable to start. We'll produce a dashboard that breaks down submetrics. Note: cost will be normalized per 1k tokens and per-embedding call where relevant.
[07:20] Ariana: Let's talk golden prompts. We'll provide a template — the idea is to pin ~25 golden prompts per pipeline that represent highest-value user flows. For each golden prompt we'll track expected fields and acceptable variations.
[08:10] Priya: We'll also include negative examples — prompts that should return ‘no result’ or ‘escalate to human’. Do you have a standard structure for negative case labeling?
[08:40] Mateo: Yes, include an "intent: escalate" label and ideally a short rationale why. Our regression harness can assert the label and the absence/presence of hallucinated entities.
[09:35] Leah: How do you detect hallucinations automatically?
[10:00] Mateo: We use a few heuristics: entity cross-checking against a ground truth table, confidence thresholds, and a lightweight semantic similarity check. We'll also run an LLM-based hallucination classifier as a second pass — that is, a model that flags likely hallucinations which then get human-reviewed. Expect some false positives, we calibrate on your golden set.
[11:20] Priya: What about format checks — we have strict JSON schemas for downstream systems. Can you validate schema and field types?
[11:45] Mateo: Yep, schema validation is built into the eval harness. We'll run strict and lenient modes — strict will fail if any field deviates, lenient will allow small formatting differences but flag them.
[12:30] Ariana: Regarding regression tests: we'll snapshot outputs from the baseline model and compare new candidate models across the golden set. We track regressions by delta in composite score and also start a regression alert if any critical field regresses beyond threshold.
[13:10] Priya: Thresholds — for us a critical field drop of more than 5% is unacceptable. For hallucination increase, anything over +2% relative to baseline is a fail.
[13:40] Mateo: We'll expose parameters so you can tune those thresholds. We'll also run A/B tests during the POC if you want to compare quantized vs fp16 variants to measure cost/quality tradeoffs.
[14:30] Samir: About cost: we need a rough estimate for the nightly run and the interactive 95th percentile — can you ballpark?
[15:00] Ariana: Ballpark depends on model choice and quantization. For example a 13B quantized model on Redwood Dedicated might run ~ $0.15 per 1k tokens for inference cost in our internal examples; smaller model would be lower. We'll provide a cost modeling spreadsheet.
[15:50] Priya: Please call out any differences between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for data residency and audit logs. We need SOC2 compliance and retention controls.
[16:20] Ariana: Absolutely — Redwood Private supports dedicated control plane and KMS; logs are available for x months depending on plan. We'll attach our security whitepaper and SOC2 summary.
[17:05] Mateo: Back to workload sizing — we recommend sampling sequence length distribution from your 200 samples; that will drive kernel selection and batching config. If you typically have 800 token docs we will size for longer KV cache and more memory.
[18:15] Priya: We have a mix: most items 150-400 tokens, but regulatory docs can be 2k+ tokens. For the POC we'll supply samples across that distribution.
[19:05] Mateo: Great. For benchmark metrics we'll capture: composite score, per-field accuracy, hallucination rate, schema pass rate, latency p50/p95/p99, tokens per second, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens.
[20:00] Leah: On timeline, can you outline milestones?
[20:15] Ariana: Milestone 1: golden prompt + samples collected (due 2026-01-17). Milestone 2: baseline run + initial report (due 2026-01-24). Milestone 3: iteration + canary test (due 2026-02-03). We'll confirm exact dates in the shared sheet.
[21:40] Priya: For the composite scoring — you mentioned a hallucination penalty. How is that computed?
[22:00] Mateo: We'll compute hallucination_rate = flagged_hallucinations / number_of_examples. Penalty is a multiplier applied to the correctness subscore; e.g., composite = correctness* (1 - alpha*hallucination_rate) where alpha is tunable (default 0.4). We'll put the math in the rubric.
[23:30] Ariana: Also note we'll include a human-in-the-loop sample of ~50 examples to sanity check classifier flags and calibrate precision/recall.
[24:10] Samir: Any need for data anonymization before upload? Some docs have PHI.
[24:35] Priya: We can provide redacted versions; we'll confirm what you need.
[25:00] Mateo: For the POC we can work with redacted data; if raw PHI is required for fidelity we can operate under Private deployment or strict NDA. We'll document options.
[26:20] Leah: Can you run a quick demo of the eval harness output and the dashboard?
[27:00] Mateo: Sure — demo gist: dashboard shows a line for composite score over time, submetric breakdown, per-example drilldowns with diffs and highlighted hallucinated spans. Example: [shows sample] — expected diagnosis: 'Type II diabetes'; model returned 'Type I' flagged as high-severity regression.
[29:10] Ariana: A few practical asks: please include a column in the report for 'business impact' — e.g., whether a regression triggers manual review or customer-facing rollback.
[29:45] Priya: Yes, that is helpful.
[30:15] Mateo: On automation: we'll wire up regression alerts to your Slack/Teams channel and open JIRA tickets when a critical regression is detected.
[31:00] Samir: Security — can Redwood sign a data processing addendum for the POC?
[31:20] Ariana: Yes, we have a standard DPA; we'll send to Samir after the call. We can also provide our SOC2 report on request.
[32:05] Priya: Are there any limitations around quantization — some of our models degrade on int8.
[32:25] Mateo: We'll test multiple quant configs during the bench: int8 dynamic, int8 static if supported, and fp16. We'll compare quality deltas on the golden set. We'll flag any regressions visible on critical fields.
[33:40] Leah: Regression cadence — how often will you snapshot models?
[33:55] Ariana: For the POC, weekly snapshots is fine. For longer engagements, daily or per-rollout snapshot is typical.
[34:30] Priya: If a model fails acceptance, what is rollback policy?
[34:50] Mateo: We recommend automatic fallback to the baseline model in production and a canary with 5-10% traffic for candidate models until cleared. We'll include automatic fallback rules in the rollout plan.
[35:40] Ari(ana): Sorry, quick note: we'll need contact for infra on your side for network whitelisting, etc. Samir?
[35:52] Samir: I'll be point for that. I'll open a ticket and share IP allowlist and VPC peering requirements.
[36:30] Priya: One more item — how do you handle multi-turn context for clinical summaries? We need KV cache to persist across turns for a session length of up to 6 turns.
[37:00] Mateo: We support cached KV contexts and you can configure max cache size and TTL. For multi-turn scoring we'll include context-aware correctness metrics.
[38:20] Leah: Anything we should be aware of regarding the eval harness being brittle to prompt paraphrases?
[38:40] Mateo: Yes — that is why we ask for prompt families. We'll group paraphrases of the same intent and mark them as equivalent in the golden set. The scorer will allow some semantic variance using embedding similarity thresholds.
[39:55] Priya: We'll also want to measure hallucination false positives from the classifier — what's acceptable?
[40:15] Mateo: For the POC we'll aim for classifier precision > 0.7 initially and then tune. Human review sample will help raise precision.
[41:10] Ariana: Recap of concrete deliverables: golden prompt template, sample ingestion spec, benchmark config, scoring rubric, security docs and DPA.
[42:00] Priya: Sounds good. Quick question about tooling — will the results be accessible via API and dashboard?
[42:20] Mateo: Yes both — dashboard and an API endpoint for per-example results and aggregate metrics. We'll give you a short token-limited access account for the POC.
[43:10] Samir: For the nightly batch we need retention of raw outputs for 30 days for audit. Is that supported?
[43:30] Ariana: Yes 30-day retention is fine, we can extend in Enterprise plans. We'll note that in the DPA.
[44:05] Leah: Any assumptions or risks we should track?
[44:20] Mateo: Main risks: sample set not representative, PHI limitations on raw data, and quantization causing model degradation. We'll call out mitigation steps for each.
[45:00] Priya: Okay let's lock dates. We'll aim to have the sample set by the 17th and expect your initial run the following week.
[45:20] Ariana: Perfect. We'll send calendar invites for the benchmark run and the follow-up debrief.
[46:00] Priya: One last technical nuance — for schema enforcement if a field is missing should that be 'fail' or 'null allowed'? We'll send an enforcement table per field.
[46:20] Mateo: We'll support both. For critical fields we'll configure 'fail' in strict mode. Non-critical can be 'nullable' and flagged.
[47:10] Ariana: Any outstanding questions?
[47:20] Leah: Not from product.
[47:30] Samir: I'll follow up on networking and DPA.
[47:45] Priya: We'll prepare the sample set and negative examples.
[48:00] Ariana: Great — thanks everyone. We'll recap and send artifacts.
[48:15] (crosstalk) everyone: thanks, bye.

Post-meeting notes: deck referenced: 'POC Eval Playbook v2' (link in CRM), security pack: 'Redwood SOC2 & DPA' (sent after call).

End transcript.
